summary: Build any m x n grid of '.' and '#' with exactly one right/down path from the top-left to the bottom-right.
mainInsight: Construct the path yourself and block everything else. Free the whole top row and the whole right column (an L shape), make every other cell '#'. With only right/down moves the L is the single path.

approaches.name: Construct an L-shaped path
approaches.summary: Top row and right column free, all else blocked.

approaches.name: Staircase path
approaches.summary: Alternate right and down moves as in the examples, blocking the rest.

commonMistakes: Leaving extra free cells that create a second path.
Counting paths with DP instead of just constructing one.
Forgetting 1 x n or m x 1 grids, where the single row/column is the path.

cards.answer: Direct construction: free one fixed path (top row then right column) and block every other cell. Clue: It asks you to return any grid with exactly one right/down path, so you may choose the path yourself and block every other cell.

promptVariants: Why does blocking every cell outside the L give exactly one path?
Why is the top-row-plus-right-column grid correct?
options: The L leaves no choice at any free cell
Blocked cells can be walked through once
The examples prove every L shape is unique
Right/down paths always have exactly one route
cards.answer: The L leaves no choice at any free cell
cards.explanation: From each free cell of the top row (except the corner) the down cell is blocked, so you must go right; on the right column the only move is down. There is never a choice.

incorrectOptionExplanations.The examples prove every L shape is uniq: Examples do not prove anything; the no-choice argument does.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Right/down paths always have exactly one: An open grid has C(m + n - 2, m - 1) paths.

promptVariants: m = 2, n = 2. What does the canonical code return?
For a 2 x 2 grid, what grid does the L construction build?
cards.explanation: Top row free, right column free, the bottom-left cell blocked: one path right then down.

incorrectOptionExplanations.[\"..\", \"..\"]: All free gives two paths (right-down and down-right).
incorrectOptionExplanations.[\".#\", \"..\"]: Also a valid single-path grid (down then right), but not what this construction builds.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[\"#.\", \"..\"]: The start cell is blocked, so there is no path at all.

promptVariants: An open m x n grid has C(m + n - 2, ___) right/down paths, which is why you must block cells.
Number of monotone paths in an open m x n grid: C(m + n - 2, ___)
cards.explanation: A path is a sequence of m - 1 downs and n - 1 rights; choose where the downs go. C(m + n - 2, m - 1) = C(m + n - 2, n - 1).

promptVariants: What is the time complexity of the canonical code?
How much work does building the grid take?
cards.explanation: Every cell of the output has to be written.

incorrectOptionExplanations.O(m + n): That is the path length, but all cells must be filled.
incorrectOptionExplanations.O(C(m + n, m)): That counts paths; the construction never enumerates them.
incorrectOptionExplanations.O(1): The output size grows with m * n.

promptVariants: The output grid itself takes O(___) space.
cards.explanation: There is no extra structure beyond the returned grid.
